title: A group principal names a powerhouse/reactor-group roster document whose membership is folded at each operation's position, so hiring and offboarding are single membership operations
content:
Who may approve an expense is a question a **roster document** answers. The expense report's policy names a `powerhouse/reactor-group` document with a `{ group: <documentId> }` principal, and the reactor folds that roster's membership — at each operation's position — whenever it decides an approval.

The roster is an ordinary document: `{ name, description, members }` state, replicated and event-sourced like everything else, and governed by its **own** auth scope (the recipe's roster is Alice-only, so Bob cannot enrol himself). Hiring and offboarding are `addMember` / `removeMember` on the roster; the referencing document's auth stream never grows — the test asserts it stays at its genesis operation — and every document that trusts the group picks the change up at its next decision.

Membership is **positional**: a `removeMember` timestamped before an already-accepted approval re-judges it. The reactor re-evaluates every document whose policy references the group, each in its own job, using the reverse direction of the group-reference relation, and the approval flips to a stored denied operation. A replica that receives the expense report but not the roster cannot fold membership, so the principal matches **nobody** and the synced approval is denied there — access is never widened by absence — and when the roster's history arrives the replica re-judges and converges verdict for verdict. The read-set is therefore a sync obligation: a grant that names a group makes that document part of what an enforcing replica must hold.

Bounds: no group can reference another group (the platform rejects `{ group }` principals on a group document's own policy), so membership never chains and the read-set stays flat; and until conditions ship, a group's own policy is limited to `address` and `anyone` principals. Group principals match only with the `authGroups` flag (third in the cascade) — below it they are skipped, which is what the disclaimers in the other auth recipes describe.
